newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS - VIX rises despite range-bound OEX.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS - VIX rises despite range-bound OEX.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. stock indices rose in early trade, despite a relatively narrow-ranged trading in the overall stock market after Tuesday's big rally, traders said.

They noted that today's gainers were led by the technology sector, which had been lagging the broader market in recent rallies, again displaying a divergence between the big caps and the small caps that has kept the market nervous.
"It's sort of a quiet-before-the-storm situation right now,' said Jesse Stamer of TradeNet, a designated primary market maker at the Chicago Board Options Exchange.
He said caution ahead of International Business Machines Corp earnings due out after the market close and the U.S. Treasury's five-year note auction subdued options volume and buoyed volatilities.

The CBOE volatility index VIX, which reflects implied volatilities for near-month S&P100 index OEX options, was up 1.14 point at 22.31 at 1140 CDT/1640 GMT. The OEX was down 1.75 at 756.15 on light option volume.
Brian Belski, a vice president at Dain Bosworth, said the market's instability was visible in the fact that only some shares were carrying the load for the gains in major indices.

"As in last week, yesterday there was a clear divergence between the big caps and the rest of the market...and today we're seeing a techs-led rally," Belski said. "Advance/declines (ratios) aren't really catching fire either."

He said the gains in the past week and a half looked more like a corrective bounce than a full-fledged rally and that implied volatilities for options were likely to stay high for a while until the market bottomed out more clearly.
On the other hand, Stamer said volatilities could stabilize once the major first-quarter earnings were out of the way, particularly IBM's.

"I think the nervousness has been over earnings," he said. "There have been several disappointments, but yet there have been several good surprises. If you get IBM showing better than expected earnings, I think you can get a good upside surge in the techs and the overall market."

Another CBOE trader said implied volatilities were roughly in line with the big intra-day movement the market has had this year and that VIX was unlikely to stay below 20 for a long time even if it slid slightly.
"The range has shifted higher," he said.

He added that the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on May 20 would eventually worry the market more, as it seemed unlikely that the Federal Reserve had finished tightening credit with its 25-basis-point hike in the Fed funds rate in March.
